utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Please take your seat. Mr. Usher, could you please make sure that the accused is brought in?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) I would like to greet everyone. Hello to the interpreters. I hope everybody can hear me. I am also greeting the members of the Prosecution team, the members of the Defence team. Good afternoon, Mr. Jelisic. I see that Witness B is already in the courtroom. Can you hear me, Witness B? Have you been able to take a rest? Do you feel comfortable?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Thank you. I'm sorry for the slight delay. The interpreters have worked very hard this morning. Judge Rodrigues has worked very hard also this morning. We've all worked very hard, in fact, so we took a few minutes more to take a bit of rest, but we may now resume our work. May I remind you that we are in public session, that the witness is under oath, and that the witness has been granted a number of protective measures. Therefore, I will ask that since we are in open session, every document be shown on the screens of the public gallery. Mr. Greaves, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Witness B, I am going to ask you some questions now on behalf of Mr. Jelisic, and I would like you to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) You will be the only counsel putting questions to the witness; is that right, Mr. Greaves?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Witness B, can I just ask you this before I start asking you some questions: If you don't understand my question, please remember to stop me and ask me to repeat it again so that you can understand it, all right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And if you want to take a pause or anything like that because you are feeling a bit upset or anything, please ask and we'll make arrangements for you to do that, all right?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness please be advised to move closer to the microphone, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Yes. I think you may need to move a little closer to the microphone, Witness B. It's not picking up your voice. Thank you very much, Mr. Usher. Witness B, I would like to ask you, first of all, about your -- I think you arrived in The Hague this week; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Since arriving in The Hague but before you began giving evidence yesterday, did you discuss that evidence with anybody?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: So you didn't spend some time with Mr. Tochilovsky and go over what you were likely to say or your statements about these incidents?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Why are you putting this question to the witness, Mr. Greaves? What is your aim?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: The next set of questions I think will make clear what my objective is, and perhaps you would be patient, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) I will try to be patient, Mr. Greaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Witness B, my next question is this: Since you gave evidence yesterday afternoon, have you discussed that evidence with anybody?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I have not, with anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'll move on now, please, if I may? I want to ask you, first of all, now about your arrival at what I think is called the Laser company on the 6th of May of 1992. Just so that we understand the setting, please, is it right that the Laser company is a bus or transport company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was on the 6th of May, not 16th of May --

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I think you may have misheard, I think I said the 6th, but your arrival at the Laser company on the 6th of May, I want to know a little bit about the physical --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 6th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: The Laser company, is that a bus company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it is a bus company. That's where the buses would come and they would leave from there, and it was called the Laser company.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And the buildings that you were taken to, was that -- I hope that you understand the difference between the two -- was that the bus station or where the buses were repaired?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, it was neither. It was a restaurant. This is where people ate.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: So this was part of the bus station where people would actually get on the bus and get off the bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. This was within the compound of the Laser company, it was this restaurant, and I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And, again, so that we can get the picture of what the building was being used for, is it right that this building was being used as a collection point for people who had been detained and who were then moved after a couple of days to some other detention facility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. That is what the building was used for.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And in your own case, you were moved to the Luka facility on the 8th of May.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: During the period in which you were held at the Laser company, were you always kept in the restaurant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I want to ask you now about the voice that you heard at the Laser company. It is right, isn't it, that you did not physically see Mr. Jelisic at the Laser company buildings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And what it comes to is that you heard a particular voice on one of the occasions -- one of the days when you were at the Laser company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I heard Goran's voice. I did not know that it was Goran, but on the 8th of May, that it was Goran.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I'm going to come back to your knowledge of Mr. Jelisic in a moment, but I just want to explore a little, if I may, the circumstances at the restaurant. Was this on the 6th of May or on one of the days following?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: On the 6th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And you were still in the restaurant building at the time when it took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: The voice that you heard on that occasion, was it inside the restaurant or was it something that you heard taking place outside the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Inside the building. I could not see outside. I was inside the building. It wasn't just me; there was quite a few of us. There were a lot of prisoners or detainees in the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I understand that, Witness B, but can I just explore it a little further? You were inside the restaurant, but from where did the voice come? Was the voice actually inside the restaurant or was the voice outside the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Inside the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, it's right, isn't it, that you had never heard that voice before that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And, indeed, you did not know Goran Jelisic from before the war at all, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Never, never in my life had I met him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And you had never heard of him either?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Never, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I want to look at the conditions inside the restaurant. Was it at night when this incident took place when you heard the voice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was night, about 8.00. There were no lights. There was some small lamp, but you couldn't really see.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: This was on the 6th of May at night, around 8.00, at least this is my best guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Well, it may be that the time doesn't matter, but in any event, it was dark outside; the only light --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Dark, dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: The only light that was present in the building was a small light which didn't enable you to see at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Not at all. Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: So just to make it clear, it is only a question of you hearing a voice; you did not see anybody who was speaking on that occasion, you physically couldn't see anybody?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I could not. No, I could not. I could only hear the voice because I did not know who it was. In fact, there were three of them. They entered --

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Three people speaking?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. The third had a rifle, and he ordered -- he was ordered to cock his rifle, to train it on us so that we wouldn't budge.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Now, I want to ask you this, please: The voice that you heard, did you hear that for a very short period, a matter of seconds, or was there a lot of conversation and speech?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was about ten to fifteen minutes, that is the time span within which this happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Would it be right to say, Witness B, that at the time when you were first taken into detention, you were confused and in a confused state having just been detained?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Who wouldn't be confused at that time? We didn't know who was coming -- to come for my house, to see these people all scared. We were helpless. We didn't know what to do. Nobody had any idea. Everybody used to live well. We were used to good living. I almost died from fear there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I'm not criticising you in any way, Witness B; you understand that. I'm just trying to establish what frame of mind you were in and how well you were able to assess the circumstances in which you found yourself; do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Of course, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you. Given that there was only -- I'm sorry. I'm sorry, I didn't mean to interrupt, Your Honour. Given that there was only a very small light which didn't enable you to see terribly well, can you tell us this, please: How were you able to see any beatings taking place or the guard pointing a gun?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I saw because there were windows, there was moonlight. Of course, you could see; it wasn't entirely dark. At any rate, he ordered the guard to cock his gun and train it on us, and then they called us one by one, and they had to stand against the wall, to spread their legs and raise their arms, and then they started beating them and then they took turns at beating them. Two or three men were beating; and some documents were taken away, they were thrown out. The man who had been beaten asked to be given back those documents, but the next day, they couldn't find them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Yesterday in evidence, you said this when you were asked about who it was who had said, "Cock your rifle and point it at them," you told the Court, "I think it was Goran Jelisic." Do you remember saying that to us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Would it be right to say that you are not sure when you say, "I think it was him"? You are not sure that it was him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I never knew this man until I saw him in the Luka camp on the 8th of May. That's when I knew that this was Goran Jelisic from Laser, and I recognised him by his voice.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's move on to another topic please, Witness B, if we may. You've described, upon your arrival at the Luka detention facility, being taken initially -- after handing your documents in, being taken to a hangar and finding there a woman. Do you remember telling us about that yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: The woman, was she a Serb or a --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: A girl, a girl, it was a girl, and it was a Serbian girl. I don't know exactly, but she was a girl. I'm not sure whether she was Serbian, but for me, it was a girl, and she was a very pretty, attractive girl.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: But was she in any kind of uniform or was she dressed in civilian clothes or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And did she tell you that she had had her breast cut off or were you able to see that or was there just simply a large bandage or wound that you could see? How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: She didn't tell it to me. She told it to everybody who was present in the hangar. Of course, you could see that the woman had breasts, and she had a bandage where the breast was. She said that the Muslims had cut off the breast. We could see that her body was normal, but we had to watch and listen to what she was saying because we were completely helpless.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did you learn the name of this person at any stage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, no, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Was this the only occasion when you saw this girl?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I saw this girl on that day when she appeared, and never again. During my time at Luka, I never saw her again there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: All right. I'd like to now ask you, please, what time of day it was that you arrived at Luka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Around 1.30 or 2.00 on the 8th of May. From Laser, we were bussed to Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And before -- I'll start again. Was it immediately after you had handed in your documents in the way that you've described? Was it immediately after that that you were taken to the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The bus stopped right by the hangar, by the door, and we went directly from the bus into the hangar. We just had to throw all the documents as we were entering. This is what we were ordered, and this is what we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Inside the hangar, was it dark inside there when you first went in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: It wasn't dark. It was daytime. It was a nice day, sunny, but to me, it was a deadly day when I realised how many people there were in the hangar. There were glass shards from the explosion when the bridge had been blown up, and so you couldn't stand. The whole floor was filled with shards. I was very surprised.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Were the doors to the hangar closed after you had gone into it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: The door was open. Both doors were wide open.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I think there are doors at both the front and the back of the building; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, no, only on one side. No, no, they were only from one side, not from the front and back.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: If Your Honours will just give me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I'd like you to look at the exhibit bundle, please, and the first photograph in that exhibit bundle.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Please go on, Mr. Greaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I can't see the witness at the moment, and I'd like to be able to see him as I ask him questions, please, because the usher is in the way. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Witness B, have you had a look at that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that that is a photograph of what might be called the front side of the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I'd like you now to look -- well, can you just help me with this. At the back of the hangar, on the opposite side from the side which we can see on that photograph, is there a railway line, a railway siding?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. There is a railway track. I believe that there are two tracks there, a double track behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I'd like you to look at two photographs, please, and before they get an exhibit number, just have a look at them, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOCHILOVSKY
utterances.text: The Prosecution would like to see the photos first because we've never seen them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) I quite agree with Mr. Tochilovsky, Mr. Greaves, and these exhibits should receive a number anyway. You are trying to impeach the witness on some very specific issues; therefore, it is necessary for the Judges and for the members of the Prosecution team to be able to refer to the photographs on the basis of which you are trying to do this, and it's very important that the Judges should be able to see these photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Of course, and I apologise if there was any discourtesy, Your Honour. I'm just anxious to make sure that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Don't worry, Mr. Greaves. But, Mr. Greaves, you have to answer a particular question I put to you at the very beginning of the cross-examination, and you haven't given me an answer. Why did you ask the witness repeatedly a certain number of questions? You told me that I had to wait for the next set of questions. I've waited, and I haven't understood your aim.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: You're entirely right, Your Honour. I'm only concerned -- I have no objection to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) I never forget the questions I put to Defence counsel, Mr. Greaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I shall remember that, Your Honour. I have no objection to the people on the Prosecution side discussing the evidence with a witness before he gives evidence, but I make it plain that I do have an objection to them speaking to a witness after he has taken the oath and before he has completed his evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Precisely. This is a very crucial issue that you are raising, Mr. Greaves, and the members of the Defence team should think about it, just as much as members of the Prosecution team, and we will have the opportunity to go back on this particular issue, I'm sure. It is a problematic issue. What should we allow the witnesses to do outside the courtroom? This is something both the Prosecution team and the Defence team should think about. The Judges are not quite sure what the best procedure should be. I'm not criticising the questions you've put to the witness earlier on. I was just trying to see what your aim was. Thank you, Mr. Greaves, for your explanation. You may now proceed. I will just take this opportunity to hand to my colleagues the pictures of the back side of the hangar, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Can I just add that the reason I passed on immediately was because the witness said that he'd spoken to nobody, and I accept that answer, and I didn't think it, in connection with this witness, of any further importance to raise the matter, and that's why I moved on and forgot to answer Your Honour's question. I will remember in future that I have to answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Witness B, I would like you just to have a look at these two photographs, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibits 2 and 3, D2 and D3.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: This is behind -- these are the railway tracks behind the hangar, from behind. The photograph was taken from the back.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not criticising you in any way, Witness B, and I want you to be clear about that. I just want to get it clear that we can see there what looks like a door at the back of the building. Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: The door is closed. These doors were locked. They were never opened.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Those doors were never opened. They are locked. I forgot to mention that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I'm not criticising you in any way. I just wanted to make it absolutely clear that there were not only doors at the front of the building but that there were doors at the back, and you say that they were closed at all times?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, there were doors there, but they were always locked, always. No one can go out through them. They only went out through that one door. This door was always locked, and there were heavy chains on them and a big lock.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. We've finished now with the photographs. They can go back to the Registry, please. You say that when you were first in the hangar, that you could see because it was daylight outside. Apart from the daylight that was lighting up the inside of the hangar, was there any lighting of any kind inside the hangar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, there wasn't. There was moonlight that gave us light. That was all.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Can I just clarify again, as far as your arrival at Luka was concerned, was it 1.30 in the afternoon or 1.30 in the middle of the night that you arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I'd like to move now to the time when you say Mr. Jelisic came and introduced himself to you. Your evidence yesterday was that his introduction was in the following terms: "My name is Goran Jelisic, known as Adolf. You will get to know me well. I am the boss here." In relation to the first part of that introduction, it's right, isn't it, that what you said to the investigators was, "My name is Goran. They call me Adolf."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to move on now to the -- I hesitate to call it a joke because it's not a joke, but the remark that was made about those whose names would be read out were to be executed, but, in fact, they were meant for release. Were there releases that took place that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: In general terms, was that the only day on which releases took place or were there other occasions when releases took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were other occasions, but on that day, most people went home. There were another two or three occasions when 10 to 20 people were released on each of those occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I'd like you to help me with some numbers, please, Witness B. Can you tell us, and I don't want an exact figure, but roughly how many people were detained with you at Luka on the first day that you were there at the outset, and then I want to know about how many were released?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Roughly, there were about 400 or 500 of us. The hangar was full. We were standing very close to one another. We were packed. There were too many of us, in fact. More than half of the hangar was packed full. We were standing right next to one another, so there really were quite a number of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Of the 400 or 500, I appreciate that's a very rough figure, but of the 400 or 500 people who were initially there, how many would you say were, in fact, released that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I assume about 100, maybe a little more. Anyway, quite a number were released because he carried quite a large number of documents with him, so did the guard, so quite a large number were released that day. Within a two-hour period after having examined those documents, these people were called out and they were released. I can't give you the exact number, but many, almost half, of the people in the hangar were released.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Help me with this: You think there were some two or three other days when releases took place, is that accurate, or was it more or less?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: On those occasions, were similar numbers of people released from the detention facility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know that Goran released them on that first day. As for the other days when people were released, between 10, 15, up to 30 men were released. On those occasions, I didn't see Goran giving these pieces of paper with signatures on them but, rather, the people who interrogated us, they gave us release papers. I too was interviewed, but I didn't have the good fortune to be released, but I was kept on because they said, "We don't have any more of these discharge papers. You will be moved to another part of the hangar or exchanged." In any event, there would be no more discharges, but, rather, a work unit would be formed. Anyway, for two or three days after that day, quite a number of people were released, up to 30 perhaps every day, and they were sent home.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Were all the people who were detained with you Muslim or were there people from other ethnic groups detained with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were some Croats as well but very few. Most of us were Muslims, and there were a few Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: The people who were released, were they all Muslim people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think, I can't be sure, but most of them were certainly Muslims. I didn't know who was a Muslim, who was a Croat, but it was mostly Muslims who were released. I don't know whether any Croats went, we didn't dare look, but mostly it was the Muslims who were released. There were very few Croats anyway there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, on that first occasion when something like half the people were released, was that Goran Jelisic, you say, who released them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know for the first day. I don't know for the other days, whether it was Goran, because the people who were interrogating us in the offices, they were giving papers. Then they would come to the hangar to say good-bye to us, saying "We're going home."

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like just to move very briefly to the death of the Zahirovic brothers about which you told us yesterday.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Zahirovic, Zahirovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I'm sorry. You have to understand that I'm not a Bosnian speaker, and I do apologise if I mispronounce the names. You will forgive me, I'm sure, Witness B.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Oh, never mind, never mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: It's right, isn't it, that you personally did not see the killing of those two men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And what you know about it is what you have been told by other people, other detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to now move to another topic, please, Witness B.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: If Your Honours will just give me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: You've described to us how that evening, the first evening that you were there, people would be invited or asked to volunteer, and some three or four people would go out of the hangar. You, yourself, were not a member of such a group that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Again, in telling us about anything that may have happened outside, you are dependent on the accounts of other people as to what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I would like to move to, please, to the killing of two men after you had cleaned -- I'm sorry, let's just pause for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Just a moment, please. I wish to consult with my colleagues. Mr. Greaves, the Judges, and I too, wish to observe that there are facts which the accused has pleaded guilty to, the murder of Huso and Smajil Zahirovic was confessed to by the accused; he plead guilty to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I have not suggested anything otherwise. Merely that he did not see the incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) But after all, you are introducing some evidence. I just wish to draw your attention to the facts that have been admitted; there is no point in insisting on them too much. That is just an observation on the part of the Judges. You may continue, Mr. Greaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I think my learned friend Mr. Londrovic has something to add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Yes, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. LONDROVIC
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Your Honours, I do apologise. It is true that the accused Jelisic has confessed regarding the Zahirovic brothers but only to the killing of one of the two brothers and not both of them, just one of the two brothers. So I do apologise. And he has, in fact, been charged with the killing of one of the brothers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Let me check the indictment. Mr. Tochilovsky, which count is it? Maybe I made a mistake; it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOCHILOVSKY
utterances.text: Can we have a couple of moments just to check it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: If Your Honour has the agreed statement of facts, I think if you look at paragraph 11 of that -- I hope you've got a copy in French rather than English -- you will see the terms in which the agreement has been made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) I apologise. I was looking at paragraph 22, Counts 16 and 17, killing of Huso and Smajil Zahirovic. Maybe I'm wrong, but under this count, mention is made of two brothers; am I wrong?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: The document which I have, which is the document that has been signed by counsel for the accused and for the Prosecution, contains a paragraph 11 which reads in the following way: "He will plead guilty to Counts 20 and 21 and admit that on about the 8th of May, 1992, he took two Muslim brothers, Huso and Smajil Zahirovic, outside of the main hangar at Luka camp and shot and killed one of them." That, as I understand it, and I see my learned friend Mr. Bowers is nodding in acknowledgement that that is the agreement that has been reached, so I conclude that that is a correct statement of the position.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOCHILOVSKY
utterances.text: That is exactly what the witness testified about yesterday, that he took two brothers and he heard the shot. So there are no inconsistencies in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And I make it clear that I'm not trying to suggest in any way that there is any inconsistency in what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) But what I am troubled by, Mr. Prosecutor, is that when we had the initial appearance on the amended indictment, when paragraph 22 was read out, I had the impression that the accused recognised his guilt. He used the same wording. I don't have the transcript before me -- maybe I am mistaken. Do you make a distinction between Counts 16 and 17 and 14 and 15? The indictment was read by the registrar as follows --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOCHILOVSKY
utterances.text: The difference between Counts 16 and 17 and Counts 15 and 14, 14 and 15, the difference is that in the first incident, Counts 14 and 15, neither the accused nor the witnesses were sure which of the two victims were killed by Goran Jelisic. So he pleaded guilty to killing one of those victims. With regard to Counts 16 and 17, again, he is charged with killing one of those brothers, and he admitted to that, killing one of those brothers. So there is no inconsistencies and no disagreements between the Defence and the Prosecution on these counts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) The difference being that the title, the title of your counts, at least in the French version, 16 and 17 say "killing of Huso and Smajil Zahirovic." If that is the case, we need to revise the text, at least the French text. I don't know what the English text says. Let me look. But in that case, it needs to be amended. Even in the English version, it says "killing of Huso and Smajil Zahirovic."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOCHILOVSKY
utterances.text: Your Honours, this indictment is not only against Goran Jelisic but also against another accused, and another accused participated in that, so we couldn't change the caption of the counts. That's what we were saying: Two victims were killed and two indictees are in this indictment. One of those victims was killed by the accused; the accused pled guilty to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Very well. In that case, we are in agreement. Without knowing which one was killed by the accused, we agree that the accused admitted killing one of the two brothers, Huso and Smajil Zahirovic, without being able to determine today who was the victim of Goran Jelisic. So things are clear now. Thank you. You may continue, Mr. Greaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Can I also point out that the particulars of the count make it plain that the allegation against him is "shot and killed one of them," so his plea that he tendered to the Court was a proper plea to the indictment on the basis which has been agreed, and I see two of my learned friends nod in agreement of my assessment of that position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) That's fine. We have no further problems. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Witness B, I'm sorry, I was going to ask you now, please, about the incident in which you saw the killing of two men after you had cleaned an office, and I'm sorry to have to go over a little bit of the details of that again. Would it be right to say that in the terms of your life, that was the most shocking thing that's ever happened to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. It was the first time for me to witness a killing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Would it be right to say that both during and after the incident, you were in a very confused and shocked state?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Of course, I was. How couldn't I have been when I saw two young men being killed half a metre away? I stood there, I was immobile, I was wet from perspiration. I couldn't believe my own eyes, seeing one man kill another. I saw this with my own eyes; it is the truth. I am telling you what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Let me make it plain to you, Witness B, that I'm not for a moment suggesting that you are in any way being other than truthful about that incident, and also that I do not in any way criticise you for being confused and shocked at such an incident. I don't want you to think that I'm making light of it in any way. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do. Please speak freely. I am here to tell the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Would it be right to say that during the incident that you described to us, that you were focused on the fact of killing that was taking place in front of your eyes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know how to answer that question. Could you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Yes. That there were two men whose lives were being put at an end, and just help us about that which you were focusing your attention on. Was it the two men who were there on the ground being killed? Was that what you were looking at in particular?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: They weren't lying on the ground. At first I was cleaning the office. There was my jacket on the traffic sign, and the traffic sign was next to the grate. I went up to it; I cleaned it well. I heard Goran's voice. I cleaned the office. I was going towards the traffic sign on which my jacket was hanging. Goran entered the hangar leading the young man, a young man, and he was going towards the grate where my jacket was. I went out to fetch my jacket, and I was struck dumb. This was the first time I saw anything like that. They reached the grate. He ordered the young man to kneel down, which he did, to put his head on the kerb, the grate was right next to the kerb, and I was standing there. I was about to pick up my jacket with my left hand, but I stopped dead, and the young man did whatever he was ordered to do. He put his forehead on the kerb, and he took out his pistol and shot him in the back of the head. The man went limp. He called for three volunteers, who had to come out of the hangar, and I watched all this, and these volunteers carried the dead man behind the shed where they would throw the bodies. While these volunteers were carrying the man, he went back to the hangar for another fair, blond man with a broken nose. He told me, "Stay there." And I did. And he told this other man too to kneel down. The young man did so. He told him to put his head, to lean his head against the kerb. The young man didn't want to do that. Again, he shouted at him, "Put your head there," and then he got hold of him with his jacket, got hold of his jacket, and pushed his head down saying, "Don't move." The poor thing had to do that, and he killed this second young man. And again he called for three volunteers, and they went out and carried him. And then he said to me, "What are you doing there?" I couldn't speak. I had a choking feeling in my throat. I was trembling. I was wet with perspiration to see two young men being killed. And so with my head and my hands, I was indicating that I was cleaning the office. And went to see. I had cleaned it well. He said, "You have cleaned it well. You won't be killed." And he said, "Why are you so scared?" Of course, I had to be scared. If I had a voice to speak with, I would have told him. And he said to me, "Since you have done the job well, you won't be killed. Go into the hangar."

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Witness B, I don't doubt the details except in one regard, and I want to ask you about that now. What I want to suggest to you is that in the confusion and shock of this incident, you made a mistake about who it was who was carrying out the killing and that, in fact, it was not the accused Goran Jelisic who did it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was Goran Jelisic. In the second case too. I saw it with my own eyes. I have him in my mind. It couldn't be anyone else but Goran, unless I had gone crazy.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Well, Witness B, just so that it's plain --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) What was the name of this victim, please? I wish to check --

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: There's been no evidence as to what the name of this person was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOCHILOVSKY
utterances.text: We don't have the name of the victim in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Very well. Please continue. Proceed, Mr. Greaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Just to conclude, I make it plain what the case for the Defendant is on this point, is that you have made a mistake as to the name of the perpetrator of this crime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Are we outside the indictment, Mr. Prosecutor? Yes, Mr. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOCHILOVSKY
utterances.text: Mr. President, in our indictment in Count 1, it reads that in addition to those killings enumerated in all these counts, he killed other people, other detainees, other victims, which are not named in those counts. It is in our Count 1. So it is within the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Thank you. So we are within the scope of the indictment. What is the detail over which you wish to question this victim, please? Are you trying to contest his version of events?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I contest it only in respect of one thing, which is as to who it was who committed these killings. I don't contest any other matter, and I make it plain both to Your Honour and to the witness that I am not calling him a liar, I am merely saying that he is mistaken, and that the reason for his being mistaken is his condition as a result of what he had seen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Very well. Your observation is a pertinent one, Mr. Greaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I am now going to refer, Your Honour, if you have got the document which is the agreed basis of plea in front of you, I am now going to refer to paragraph 14 of that, and I think Your Honours will find it on page 5 of the English version. I'm not sure of the French version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Which paragraph, Mr. Greaves?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Paragraph 14.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Mr. Greaves, I don't have this document at the moment. At any rate, we are going to take a 15-minute break. This will give me the opportunity to find this document, and I don't wish to go any further on this issue. I will only enter this debate once I have the French version of this basis of plea in French. We are going to take a break. As I was saying, a 15-minute break. This will give the registrar the opportunity to hand me the French version of this basis of plea, and then you can proceed, Mr. Greaves, with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) The hearing is resumed. Can the accused be brought in, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Mr. Greaves, thanks to the Registrar's efforts, the Judges now have the French version of the agreed basis of plea. You were referring us to paragraph 14; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, paragraph 14.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) The murder of Stipo Glavocevic; is that right, Mr. Greaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: That's the one I'm referring to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Witness B, I want to turn now to the incident in which a man returned to the hangar with an ear which had been cut off, and I think you will recall having told us about that incident yesterday.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: (Nodding)

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Can I just remind you of this: The court reporters can't write down just a nod. It will be helpful if you say "Yes" or "No" to each question. Can you remember to do that, please, Witness B?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I said "Yes."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) The court reporters are extremely efficient, Mr. Greaves, and they specify when the witness nods or makes a gesture, but it is preferable, of course, for the witness to speak out loud when answering your questions. Witness B, please try to make an effort and speak out.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: The man whom you told us about, do you know his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did you subsequently learn it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I later learned it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the name of that man was Stipo or Stjepo Glavocevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Stipo, even though I did not know this man at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: But that was the name that you subsequently learned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, from those who knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Witness B, you described how, during the course of the incident, Mr. Jelisic said, "You are not people. You are nothing. You should all be killed." It's right, isn't it, that --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: -- it's right, isn't it, that you told the investigators that what he said was, "You are not men. You are afraid to kill him. I should kill you all." Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, he said that. He was giving us a pistol to kill him but we didn't dare.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And what I want to go on to ask you is this: That after Goran had said that, the man Stipo said, "Brothers, friends, please kill me. I prefer you to kill me than these criminals," and that's what you told the investigators?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's how I said it. He begged us. He said, "Brothers, Muslims, or if there are any Croats here, I prefer that any of you kill me than this criminal," and then Goran offered each one of us his pistol to kill him, and then he said, "What kind of people are you? You can't kill your own even."

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Witness B, I want to turn now to the killing of the man called Ismail Rebic and the Serb who were together. Again, in the case of that incident, it's right, isn't it, that you, yourself, did not witness the killing of either of those two men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And again in relation to those matters, the killing of either of those two men, you rely on what others have told you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, those who carried out those bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Do you accept that you told investigators in relation to that matter that someone killed them, implying that you did not know who it was who had done it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not see with my own eyes, but they were killed and they were taken out.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: So you don't know who did it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know. I did not see it with my own eyes, but they were killed and they were carried out. I washed the blood away.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness B. I want now to explore with you, if we may, please, the time scale within which all the incidents which you have told us about happened. Would you accept that, having arrived on the 8th of May at Luka detention camp, all the incidents of killing and mistreatment which you saw took place within -- about which you've told us yesterday, all those incidents took place within ten days of your arrival. Would you accept that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I want to turn now to the incident when a captain came to the camp and some orders were read out to you. You will recall telling us that someone you described as a captain came to the camp, and Jelisic read out some orders to you. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I remember that well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: May I assume that you are of an age where you would have done your national service in the former JNA some years before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I'm familiar with the length of service. How long do you have to do -- how long does national service take out of your life? Is it 18 months, two years?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Eighteen months, that is what I served.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Were you in a regular infantry unit or what sort of unit were you in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't need to say that. I was a soldier. That's what's important.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I simply want to just know how you're able to recognise the different uniforms of the JNA. That's all I'm after. I'm not after any personal details, Witness B. I just want to know how you knew it was a captain. Let's put it this way: You're familiar with all the uniforms and the ranks of the army; is that fair?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: For me, he was a military officer, and I believe he had three stars, so that would make him a captain, but in any event, he was an officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Can you give us any better description of the man, the captain, what sort of age he was, his appearance, his size?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was dark. He may have been about 180 centimetres tall, and I don't know what else. He was good looking.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: What sort of age was he, young, old, compared with yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: He wasn't young; he wasn't old. He was 35 to 40 maybe. But at any rate, he was not young or old. He was in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: The uniform -- I'm sorry. I didn't let you finish and I apologise. The uniform he was wearing, Witness B, was that a formal uniform or a combat uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, it was not a combat uniform. It was a regular officer's uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did he speak to the assembled people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Is this correct, that he was there supervising the reading out of the orders by Mr. Jelisic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know that he was there with Goran. He stood there. Goran read it out. We listened. He read it out. We didn't know whether to believe it or not, but it turned out to be true, what Goran read. No person was killed in Luka by gunshot after that. There were some people later on who succumbed to beatings, but there was not a single person who was killed by a bullet after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: What time of day was the visit of this captain and the reading out of these orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: This was in the morning, around 8.00, I couldn't tell you exactly, but around that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Had you ever seen the captain before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I had not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did you ever see him again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, no, after he left, I never saw him again, ever.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Were he and Mr. Jelisic already there when you were assembled or did they come in or what? Can you just describe how they arrived to come and give this information to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Jelisic entered, and he walked in with him on his right. We lined up. Jelisic read it out, and the officer just stood there observing. When Jelisic finished reading, they both turned about and left the hangar. He said nothing. He just observed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Did the captain give Mr. Jelisic the document to read out to you? Did you see him do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, Goran had it in his hand. It was in Goran's hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Can you just help us with this: Other members of the staff of the detention facility, did you have an opportunity to see them on a regular basis?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: What staff?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: By "staff," I mean guards and the personnel who were in charge of the camp, apart from Mr. Jelisic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was just Goran and this officer who entered the hangar. The guards were outside. I only saw the two of them, and Goran read out from this paper, and they left. The officer never spoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Witness B, it's my fault entirely, and I do apologise. I did not ask that question well. I'm going to ask it again. In general terms, apart from Mr. Jelisic, when you were in the camp, did you see other personnel who were part of the camp staff --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: -- on days other than this or did you only see Mr. Jelisic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. Jelisic was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Were there other guards, apart from Mr. Jelisic, not on this particular day but in general, in the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were guards, of course. When Jelisic was not around, there were guards around --

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: From what --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: -- and the warden was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: From what you were able to see, was the captain part of the staff of the camp or had he come from somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: He wasn't part of the staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, he wasn't. I saw him for the first time, and after he left, I never saw that man again.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Can you help us to try and fix the date on which this incident took place, when the captain came? Again, would that be within ten days of your arrival at the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: If you were able to fix it more precisely than that, what date would you say it was, the 17th, 18th of May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I believe so because I was there on the 18th, and it wasn't late. I know it was in May. It must have been either the 17th or the 18th, one of those two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I want to turn very briefly now to the time when you were in the camp at Batkovic, Witness B. You told the Court yesterday that at some date in September you saw Mr. Jelisic at Batkovic camp. What I want to suggest to you is that you're mistaken about having seen Mr. Jelisic at Batkovic camp.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I am not mistaken. I saw him. I was lying down, and I saw him when he came to hangar 2. He was first in hangar 1 looking for people from Brcko who had been there in May at Luka. I was not in that hangar. Then he moved to hangar 2 where I was, and we were there. We heard that he had been down there, and then he entered the hangar and asked whether there were any people from Brcko who were in the camp in May. The guards said that there were none, that all had been exchanged, and he said, "It is not possible that there are none left," and they repeated, "Yes, they were all exchanged." We kept on lying on the ground. Goran was well-known. I recognised him by his voice. He was looking for the people from Brcko, and he was asking, "How come there are none from Brcko," and the guards said, "No, all of those who were at Luka had been exchanged," and then he left.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Do you accept, Witness B, that you didn't mention the visit of Mr. Jelisic to the Batkovic camp to the investigators in this case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: The question is not clear to me. What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: What I'm suggesting to you is that you didn't tell the investigators about that incident and that it's not recorded by them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Just a second. I need to consult with my colleagues, Mr. Greaves. Mr. Greaves, we are somewhat concerned. It's not the first time you've gone over what has been or what has not been said to the investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor. Remember that what is most important for the Judges is to have elements which enable them to establish the truth. Yesterday before us, the witness stated that Goran Jelisic, the accused, came to the Batkovic camp. He just explained to you what has happened. You are allowed to contradict this particular point, but we have already gone over this point a number of times. It is a very important issue, but it's not the key issue in this case. Would you please try to put your question to the witness in another way? If you want to contest his answer, please tell us why and try to explain. The other thing we would like to specify is that we would like this cross-examination to be over quickly because remember that we are not sitting tomorrow or Friday, and we wouldn't like this witness to have to come back in January. Do remember that the Judges will have some questions to put to the witness. It is now 4.25; we will work until 6.30, more or less. We have two hours left. We will need to take another 20-minute break at some point. This leaves us with one hour and 40 minutes. So that's not that much time. Don't worry so much about what has been said by the witness to the investigators. Please focus on how you would like to explain the fact that you think that the witness is not saying precisely what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Your Honour, his answer has been that he doesn't accept my proposition. I'm going to move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Excellent. The Judges will decide on that particular issue at the relevant time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And if I can reassure Your Honour, I am anticipating finishing well within the time that you specified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Excellent. Thank you, Mr. Greaves. My colleagues and myself thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Witness B, I would like to move now, please, to the interrogation that was conducted with you. Was it only on one occasion that you were interrogated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Perhaps you can help us about the time scale. Were you interrogated immediately upon arrival or within a short space of time after your arrival?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Within two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: It must have been the 10th or 11th.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I apologise. I interrupted you. Whereabouts in the camp were you interrogated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the office across from where we were kept.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: On that occasion, how long did the interrogation last for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: The first time, it lasted about 15 minutes; and the second time, it was similar. I was saying why we had stayed behind, whether we had weapons. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Can I just take each one at a time? Who was it who conducted the first interrogation? Was it one person alone or more than one person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: There were three persons. I knew one of them but not the other two.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Who was the person whom you knew?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can't say the name right now because it has been six or seven years now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: It's in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: It may be that it doesn't matter, but how had you known the person? Was he someone you had come across in your business, or how had you known him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was from Brcko. He was from Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Was he a member of the military or a police officer or what was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know. He wore civilian clothes. He did not wear a military uniform; just civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: What about the other two; were they in uniform of any kind or were they also civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: All three wore civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: You very briefly touched on the sort of questions that you were asked. Would it be right that you were asked if you were a member of the SDA, for example?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, we were asked, and I told him that I was not, since I was not. I was in SDP. I told them like it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting otherwise. I just want to know what the nature of the questions was. Can I just move back slightly? Can I perhaps refresh your memory with the name Dragica; would that be the name that you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Dragica, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Dragica. Thank you. Were some of the questions also as to whether you had been a member of any military unit such as the Green Berets or a resistance unit of some kind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was not asked that. Dragica just asked me, "How come you stayed behind at home? Do you have weapons?" And I told him that I did not because I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: So they were interested in what your activities had been before the war and what activities you may have been involved in --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: -- but your answer was that you hadn't been involved in anything of that sort?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: In nothing of any kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Can I now ask you about the second interrogation? Can you fix a date for that? How soon after the first one was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: The first one was, I think, on the second day, and Kole was the interrogator. I know him by the name of Kole. He interrogated me like Dragica did, why we had stayed behind, whether we had weapons. I said we didn't. I said we had stayed because I didn't believe there would be a war. I stayed in my home to save what little I had because I thought it would be over quickly, like in Bijeljina. I had no weapons. I never had any weapons nor did it ever occur to me to obtain any. And this Kole offered me fruit juice. I had it. I was telling them the truth. I told them why I had stayed. I didn't believe there would be a war. I sent my wife and children to the village and I stayed at home. And he said to me, this Kole, that there were no more discharge papers and that I would be going to the other part of the hangar where we would wait to be exchanged and to work in a work unit, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I was asking if you can give us an approximate date how soon after the first interrogation did the second one take place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think it was the 12th or the 13th because there were two interrogations on two consecutive days, one after the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Was this man Kole, was he alone on that occasion or were there other people with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: He was the director at the time, and there were some others there, but I don't know any of them. They were sitting with him and questioning. They were very good to us. They asked us to tell the truth, and that is what I did. I told them the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And when you say there were others, how many others were sitting there with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Two or three men, soldiers, but they didn't interfere in the questioning. They just sat there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to turn now, please, Witness B, if I may, to the last occasion when you saw Mr. Jelisic in Luka detention camp. Is this correct, that whilst you were at the camp, he was replaced by a man called Vojkan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And Vojkan himself was replaced within about two or three days by another person called Kosta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: It may be that you don't know the answer to this question, but if you do, please help us: Are you able to say who it was who caused, first of all, Mr. Jelisic to be replaced?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Was there any talk in the camp amongst the prisoners about how he had come to be replaced?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: We knew, when Vojkan came in, he was a good young man, a good-looking one. I would like to kiss that man. He consoled us and he was the best, but he wasn't there with us for long. He was replaced immediately because they saw that he was always with us in the hangar. He encouraged us. He said he had spent his whole life with Muslims. He was a very good young man. I would love to see that Vojkan again because he was a father and a mother to us. When he entered, we would all gather round him like children and he would encourage us, try to keep our spirits up, this Vojkan, and because he was so good with us, they replaced him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: When you say "they," who do you mean by "they" and how do you know --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Major Vojkan. I know the man. I watched him. He was always with us, this Vojkan.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Vojkan was a military officer, was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know, but I know that they called him Major Vojkan, and the most important thing for me is that he was a good man.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: You told us just a moment or two ago that "they" replaced him. Who do you mean by "they"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know who replaced him. We were in the hangar. And what was happening, I don't know. I can't tell you who replaced him when I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Was there any conversation amongst your fellow detainees about that issue, as to how he had come to be replaced?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know. How could we know? All that we know is when somebody comes in and introduces himself and says, "I am so and so. As of today, you have to do as I tell you" because they changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Would you accept that the departure of Mr. Jelisic from Luka detention camp was at about the same time as or shortly after the captain had been there and orders were given not to kill anybody anymore? Would that be right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know. Goran would come again, but there was no more killing with bullets. He would come to the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I just ask you this finally, please: During the time that you were at Luka detention facility, is this right, that as far as you know, he was not always in the camp; in other words, he didn't stay there permanently, there were times when he was out of the camp? If you don't know the answer to that, just say that you don't know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Are you asking me about Goran?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Witness B.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: He wasn't there all the time. He would go into town. He would come by. That's all I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Finally, Witness B, I want to ask you about three particular individuals. First of all, a man called Ivan, who had a ponytail. Did you know such a person in the camp as a member of the personnel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: He had a ponytail. I didn't know his name was Ivan. We called him Cupo. He had long hair tied up at the back. So it is for the first time now that I hear that name.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: It may be that I've got the name wrong, but certainly there was somebody with a ponytail called Cupo; that's what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: What was his role in the camp? Was he a guard, an officer, or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can't tell you. He wasn't there all the time in Luka, but he would come in. He was terrible. He appeared to have a slight limp. He went around arrogantly and he would beat some of the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: I don't want you to go into the detail of what this particular man did, I just simply want to establish that he was there and that he took part in some of the mistreatment of prisoners. All right, Witness B? Can I ask you now about another man called Miroslav? Was there a guard or member of the personnel called Miroslav that you were aware of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't remember that name at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: All right. And the third one I want to ask you about was a man called Sok. Do you remember him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Sok?

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: And I think possibly his first name may have been Enver.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: What was his position, as far as you could see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: He wasn't like Cupo. He also beat people in the hangar. I was surprised to learn that his name was Enver because that is a Muslim name, so I assumed, I don't know what, but I was surprised to learn that his name was Enver because he also beat people in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: If Your Honours could give me a moment, please? Your Honour, those are all the questions that I have. Can I thank Witness B and wish him a safe journey home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Thank you, Mr. Greaves. I should now like to turn to the Prosecutor. Mr. Tochilovsky, would you like to exercise your right to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOCHILOVSKY
utterances.text: No, the Prosecution doesn't have any further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Thank you. In that case, I turn to my colleagues. Judge Riad, do you have any questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Yes, Mr. President. Thank you. Good afternoon, Witness B. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: (Interpretation) I have several questions for you but global ones. You have stated that Mr. Jelisic considered himself to be the most powerful person in the world, at least in Brcko this was evident.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I do. In Brcko, in Luka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Very well. So the others obeyed him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: Everybody had to obey him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: (Interpretation) And during the cross-examination, you expressed some reserve with regard some of the killings. You said that you learnt from others, those who carried the bodies, that it was Jelisic who did the killing, but you yourself didn't see that. And these others -- and according to the doubt expressed by the Defence counsel that it may not have been Jelisic, those who killed -- could they have been Jelisic's subordinates or people coming from outside? Could it have been under his orders or under somebody else's orders, against Jelisic's will, shall we say, or other colleagues' of his?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know. Whoever carried that body -- I carried four bodies and I saw Goran four times, and whoever carried bodies said that it had been Goran, that he was there by the body. Nobody saw anybody else doing the killings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Did he have any people to assist him and who he gave orders to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: (Interpretation) You also said during the cross-examination that you heard the voice of Jelisic, if I recall well, when he was giving orders to somebody to prepare their pistols.
